body.translated_text: Homage to the Blessed <s>Āryamahāgaṇapatihṛdaya</s> (Heart of the Noble Great Gaṇapati)! Homage to the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels)!

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma / gṛdhrakūṭaparvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdham ardhatrayodaśabhir bhikṣuśataiḥ saṃbahulaiś ca bodhisatvair mahāsatvaiḥ / tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma //
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), twelve hundred and fifty <s>bhikṣus</s>, and with many <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> (great beings). Then at that time, the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

body.text: yaḥ kaścit kulaputra ānanda imāni gaṇapatihṛdayāni dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati tasya sarvāṇi kāryasiddhāni bhaviṣyanti //
body.translated_text: "O <s>Ānanda</s>, whatever son of good family will retain, recite, master, and propagate these hearts (essence-spells) of <s>Gaṇapati</s>, for him all undertakings will be accomplished."

body.text:
oṃ namo 'stu te mahāgaṇapataye svāhā /
oṃ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ /
oṃ namo gaṇapataye svāhā /
oṃ gaṇādhipataye svāhā /
oṃ gaṇeśvarāya svāhā /
oṃ gaṇapatipūjitāya svāhā /
oṃ kaṭa kaṭa maṭa maṭa dara dara vidara vidara hana hana gṛhṇa gṛhṇa dhāva dhāva bhañja bhañja jambha jambha tambha (Gph_11) tambha stambha stambha moha moha deha deha dadāpaya dadāpaya dhanasiddhi me prayaccha /
oṃ rudrāvatārāya svāhā /
oṃ adbhutavindukṣubhitacittamahāhāsam āgacchati /
mahābhayamahābalaparākramāya mahāhastidakṣiṇāya dadāpaya svāhā /
oṃ namo 'stu te mahāgaṇapataye svāhā /
oṃ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ /
oṃ namo gaṇapataye svāhā /
oṃ gaṇeśvarāya svāhā /
oṃ gaṇādhipataye svāhā /
oṃ gaṇapatipūjitāya svāha /
oṃ suru suru svāhā / oṃ turu turu svāhā / oṃ muru muru svāhā /
body.translated_text:
<s>Oṃ</s>, homage to you, O great <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Oṃ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ</s>!
<s>Oṃ</s>, homage to <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Oṃ</s>, to the lord of the <s>gaṇas</s> (hosts), <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Oṃ</s>, to <s>Gaṇeśvara</s> (Lord of the Hosts), <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Oṃ</s>, to him who is worshipped by <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Oṃ kaṭa kaṭa maṭa maṭa dara dara vidara vidara hana hana gṛhṇa gṛhṇa dhāva dhāva bhañja bhañja jambha jambha tambha tambha stambha stambha moha moha deha deha dadāpaya dadāpaya</s> — grant me the <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) of wealth!
<s>Oṃ</s>, to the incarnation of <s>Rudra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Oṃ</s>, he comes with a wondrous, agitated mind and a great laugh!
To him of great terror, great strength, and great valor, to him whose <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (offering) is a great elephant — cause (him) to give, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Oṃ</s>, homage to you, O great <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Oṃ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ</s>!
<s>Oṃ</s>, homage to <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Oṃ</s>, to <s>Gaṇeśvara</s> (Lord of the Hosts), <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Oṃ</s>, to the lord of the <s>gaṇas</s> (hosts), <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Oṃ</s>, to him who is worshipped by <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
<s>Oṃ suru suru svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ turu turu svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ muru muru svāhā</s>!

body.text: yaḥ kaścit kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bhikṣur vā bhikṣuṇī vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā / yaḥ kaścit kāryam ālabhate mantrasādhanaṃ vā triratnapūjaṃ vā deśāntaragamanaṃ vā rājakulagamanaṃ vā antardhānaṃ vā tena buddhabhagavatāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā āryagaṇapatihṛdayaṃ saptavārānucārayitavyaṃ sarvakāryāṇi tasya sidhyante nātra śaṃsayaḥ / sarvakalikalahamardamātsareṣu nityaṃ śamatavyaṃ sarvapraśamaṃ gacchati / dinedine kalpam utthāya sarvasaptavārānucārayitavyaṃ mahāsaubhāge bhaviṣyati / (Gph_12) rājakulagamanakāle mahāprāsādo bhaviṣyanti / śrutidharo bhaviṣyati / na cāsya kāye mahāvyādhayo bhaviṣyanti / na kaścid eva tārapradakṣiṇo 'vatāraṃ lapsyate bhṛṅgo 'vatāraṃ lapsyati na cāsya bodhicittottarāyā bhaviṣyanti / jātau jātau jātismaro bhaviṣyati //
body.translated_text: "Whatever son of good family, or daughter of good family, or <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), or <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun), or <s>upāsaka</s> (male lay devotee), or <s>upāsikā</s> (female lay devotee) — whoever undertakes any task, whether <s>mantra</s> practice, worship of the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels), traveling to another region, going to a royal court, or becoming invisible — having made offerings to the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, one should recite the <s>Āryagaṇapatihṛdaya</s> (Heart of the Noble Gaṇapati) seven times. All undertakings will be accomplished for that person; there is no doubt about this. In all quarrels, disputes, conflicts, and jealousies, one should always pacify (them); everything will be pacified. Rising each and every day at the proper time, one should recite (the spell) seven times; one will attain great good fortune. At the time of going to the royal court, great honor will result. One will become a retainer of sacred learning. Great diseases will not arise in one's body. No one going around the stars will obtain descent (i.e., gain power over one), but a bee will obtain descent (i.e., only the humblest being). And one's <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) will not deteriorate. In birth after birth, one will remember past lives."

body.text: idam avocat bhagavān āttamanās te ca bhikṣavas te bodhisatvā mahāsatvāḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragaruḍagandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. Those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> (great beings), and the entire assembly with joyful minds, together with the world of <s>devas</s> (gods), humans, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s>, rejoiced in the words spoken by the Blessed One.
The <s>Āryamahāgaṇapatihṛdaya</s> (Heart of the Noble Great Gaṇapati) is completed.
